steps.title: Create a public connection, not an internal token
steps.detail: In the Notion Developer portal, create a new public connection. Choose installation scope, Any workspace or Selected workspaces only, at creation. This cannot be changed later.
steps.blockerTip: An internal connection token works only in your own workspace. For customers, you need a public OAuth connection.

steps.title: Set capabilities and redirect URIs
steps.detail: Set capabilities in the connection settings, for example Content Read, Update, or Insert, Comment, and User information. Add your redirect URIs under OAuth configuration.
steps.blockerTip: Notion does not take a scope query parameter. Capabilities are set in the dashboard, and page access is picked by the user at install.

steps.title: Send the user to the authorize URL
steps.detail: Send the user to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type code, owner user, and state. The user picks pages and databases to share.
steps.blockerTip: The redirect URI must match the one registered. A mismatch stops the flow.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens
steps.detail: Exchange the code at https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token with Basic auth using client ID and client secret, grant_type authorization_code, code, and redirect_uri. Store access and refresh tokens per user, server side.
steps.blockerTip: Never exchange the code in browser code. The secret must stay server side.

steps.title: Test with shared pages only
steps.detail: Test with pages the user actually shared. Unshared content is not available, even if the token works.
steps.blockerTip: A working token does not mean all pages are available. Check what was shared at install.
